key_insight: Pressure-tuned ferroelectric LaMoN$_3$ stays stable up to 40 GPa while its bandgap, excitons, and nonlinear optical response can be engineered to improve photovoltaic performance.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies pressure windows that optimize both conventional absorption and shift-current-based bulk photovoltaic action, suggesting a route to multi-junction solar absorbers with complementary mechanisms.
method: DFT/DFPT to assess structural stability and phonons under pressure
G$_0$W$_0$ and BSE to compute bandgap, exciton binding, and optical response
Tight-binding model to analyze nonlinear shift current behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an indirect G$_0$W$_0$@PBE bandgap reduction from 2.17 eV at 0 GPa to 1.45 eV at 40 GPa, with SLME improving and shift current peaking near 15 GPa.
watch_item: The results are theoretical and depend on applying high pressure, so practical device integration must address synthesis, stability, and pressure-transfer feasibility.
paper_title: Harnessing Linear and Nonlinear Optical Responses in Ferroelectric LaMoN$_3$ for Enhanced Photovoltaic Efficiency
